parts.text: We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the BEAT<

> project, focusing on urban accessibility, inclusive design, and Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). This 4-year PhD will focus on collecting and making sense of data on experienced, everyday mobility barriers, and co-designing human-centric interventions with project stakeholders.

BEAT Project: The BEAT project examines urban mobility from the lived experience of people with physical and cognitive diversity (PaCD), focusing on their complete daily mobility journey rather than isolated transportation modes or single barriers. The project investigates how mobility obstacles affect people's routines, frustrations, and personal, social, and professional lives.

BEAT has two main objectives: (1) collaboratively understand informal urban mobility barriers, their impacts, and priority areas to address, and (2) co-design and evaluate innovative solutions using AI, urban design, and policy interventions. Proposed solutions include accessible technologies like real-time accessibility maps and wearable devices, tactical urbanism, inclusivity assessment tools, and policy guidelines. The project will establish a Living Lab as a collaborative platform with target communities to identify problems and co-design and test solutions together.

Position Overview: We are seeking a motivated PhD candidate to work on inclusive mobility, accessibility, co-design, human-centered AI, and interactive technologies. The ideal candidate should be passionate about identifying urban mobility barriers and co-designing platforms that raise awareness and facilitate behavior change, while collaborating directly with people with physical and cognitive diversity (PaCD) and stakeholders through the BEAT Living Lab. The PhD will involve collecting data on everyday mobility barriers, co-designing user-centered interventions with Living Lab members, and developing information platforms to identify accessibility problems and help target groups address them. Key activities include gathering data on accessibility barriers in Living Lab cities, identifying design requirements, and co-designing awareness tools aimed at people with PaCD, policymakers, and designers.

Job Requirements: The successful PhD candidate will have:

* Master's degree (or equivalent) in HCI, urban planning, urban analytics, computational social sciences, citizen science, or a related field.
* Fluency in Dutch is recommended but not mandatory.
* Proficiency in written English.
* Strong interest in accessibility, assistive technology, human-computer interaction, and co-design research.
* Ability and willingness to work in a multi-disciplinary and multi-stakeholder team, including working with people and communities living with disabilities.
* Prior publications and experience in aforementioned research areas are assets but not a requirement.

Conditions for Employment: Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , increasing from Promovendus gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a full-time contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. The salary range will be in between € 3,059 – € 3,881.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customizable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.
